title: Mon, ma, mes…
en: Possessives (my, your, his, her, our, their)
intro: To say *my father, her brother, our family*, French uses possessives. The big difference from English: they agree with the **thing owned** (masculine, feminine or plural), not with the owner.

cases.label: mon, ma, mes — my
cases.rule: **mon** + masculine, **ma** + feminine, **mes** + plural: *mon père, ma mère, mes parents*.

cases.label: ton, ta, tes — your (tu)
cases.rule: Same pattern for someone you call **tu**: *ton frère, ta sœur, tes cousins*.

cases.label: son, sa, ses — his / her
cases.rule: **son / sa / ses** mean both *his* and *her*: *son père, sa mère, ses enfants*.

cases.label: notre, nos — our
cases.rule: **notre** + one thing (masculine or feminine), **nos** + plural: *notre famille, nos enfants*.

cases.label: votre, vos — your (vous)
cases.rule: **votre** + one thing, **vos** + plural — for **vous** (polite, or several people).

cases.label: leur, leurs — their
cases.rule: **leur** + one thing, **leurs** + plural: *leur fils, leurs enfants*. Both sound the same.

cases.label: mon amie — before a vowel
cases.rule: Before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, use **mon / ton / son**, not *ma / ta / sa*: *mon amie, son école*.

cases.label: agrees with the thing, not the owner
cases.rule: *Hugo et sa mère* = Hugo and **his** mother. *Léa et son père* = Léa and **her** father. Only the noun after it counts.

cases.label: de + name = 's
cases.rule: French has no **'s**: *le frère de Léa* = Léa's brother. Before a vowel: *le père d'Inès*.

sections.title: 1. My, your, his / her

examples.en: His (or her) children live in Lyon.

sections.tip: **mes, tes, ses** all end in the sound /e/. Before a vowel you hear a /z/: *mes‿enfants* /me.zɑ̃.fɑ̃/.

sections.title: 2. Our, your, their
sections.tip: With *notre, votre, leur*, masculine or feminine doesn't matter — only one or several.

sections.title: 3. His or her? Look at the noun
text: English picks *his* or *her* from the owner. French picks **son / sa / ses** from the noun that follows.
sections.tip: *son père* can mean *his father* or *her father* — the situation tells you which.

sections.title: 4. Before a vowel: mon amie
text: **ma, ta, sa** can't go before a vowel sound. Use **mon, ton, son** instead, even for a feminine noun.

sections.title: 5. Léa's brother: de + name
text: French has no **'s**. Say “the brother of Léa”: **le frère de Léa**. Before a vowel, **de** becomes **d'**: *la mère d'Inès*.

examples.fr: {Les parents de Tom|pos-de} habitent à Londres.

mistakes.why: **mère** is feminine → **sa**, even though Hugo is a man.
**père** is masculine → **son**, even though Léa is a woman.
No **'s** in French: **le frère de Léa**.
After **mes**, the noun is plural: add a (silent) **-s**.

lines.fr: C'est {le mariage de Chloé|pos-de}, la cousine de Léa et de Hugo.
lines.en: It's Chloé's wedding — Léa and Hugo's cousin.

lines.fr: Léa, c'est qui, l'homme avec Chloé ? C'est {son mari|pos-his-her} ?
lines.en: Léa, who's the man with Chloé? Is that her husband?

lines.fr: Oui ! Il s'appelle Karim. Et la femme, là, c'est {sa mère|pos-agree}.
lines.en: Yes! His name is Karim. And the woman there is his mother.

lines.fr: Ils sont là, avec {leur fils|pos-their} Jules et {leurs amis|pos-their}.
lines.en: They're there, with their son Jules and their friends.

lines.fr: Bonjour, les enfants ! Vous êtes de la famille de Chloé ?
lines.en: Hello, children! Are you part of Chloé's family?

lines.fr: Oui, madame. Chloé, c'est {notre cousine|pos-our}. Et voici {mon frère|pos-my}, Hugo.
lines.en: Yes, madam. Chloé is our cousin. And this is my brother, Hugo.

lines.fr: Enchantée ! Et {vos parents|pos-your-pl}, ils sont là ?
lines.en: Nice to meet you! And your parents, are they here?

lines.fr: Oui, {notre père|pos-our} et {notre mère|pos-our} sont avec {nos grands-parents|pos-our}.
lines.en: Yes, our father and our mother are with our grandparents.

lines.fr: Très bien ! Moi, je suis la grand-mère de Karim. {Mon fils|pos-my}, c'est {son père|pos-agree}.
lines.en: Very good! I'm Karim's grandmother. My son is his father.

lines.fr: Léa voit Sophie, {son amie|pos-vowel} de Paris.
lines.en: Léa sees Sophie, her friend from Paris.

lines.fr: Sophie ! Tu es là avec {ton frère|pos-your} ?
lines.en: Sophie! Are you here with your brother?

lines.fr: Non, avec {ma sœur|pos-my} et {mon amie|pos-vowel} Inès.
lines.en: No, with my sister and my friend Inès.

lines.fr: Et {tes parents|pos-your} ? Ils sont à Paris ?
lines.en: And your parents? Are they in Paris?

lines.fr: Oui. Mais {ta famille|pos-your} est très sympa ! J'aime bien {ton cousin|pos-your} Jules…
lines.en: Yes. But your family is really nice! I quite like your cousin Jules…

quiz.en: Is that your sister? (to a friend)
Your cousins are nice! (to a friend)
Paul and Anne love their daughter.

quiz.why: Before a vowel: **mon amie**, never *ma amie*.

quiz.en: Sophie is with her friend Inès.

quiz.q: Hugo et ___ mère sont à Lyon.
quiz.en: Hugo and his mother are in Lyon.
